title: Coordinate swap identity for an affine remainder
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $a_0\in\mathbb R$ and $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in\mathbb R$, and let $i,j$ be distinct coordinates in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. For a sign vector $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, write $x^{(ij)}_k=x_{(ij)(k)}$, where $(ij)$ swaps $i$ and $j$, and interpret each sign as its real value. The sum $a_0+\sum_{k\ne i}a_k x^{(ij)}_k$ equals $a_0+\sum_{k\notin\{i,j\}}a_k x_k+a_jx_i$.
hypotheses_covered: $a$ assigns a real coefficient to each of the $n$ coordinates
$x$ is a sign vector of length $n$
